Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 1–12:

Explanation of the words:

Yā Sīn: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa). It is written thus, يسۤ, and pronounced Yā-Sīn. Allah knows best what He intends by it.

Wal-Qur'ān al-Ḥakīm: That is, the Qur'an that possesses wisdom, for the Qur'an places everything in its proper place. It is therefore wise (ḥakīm) and also firmly structured (muḥkam) in its wondrous arrangement and marvellous meanings.

Innaka lamina al-mursalīn: That is, O Muhammad, you are among the messengers whom We sent to their peoples.

ʿAlā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm: That is, upon a straight path, which is Islam.

Tanzīla al-ʿazīzi al-raḥīm: That is, the Qur'an is a revelation from the Mighty (al-ʿazīz) in His retribution against those who disbelieve in it, the Merciful (al-raḥīm) toward those who turn to Him in repentance.

Mā unndhira ābāʾuhum: That is, their forefathers were not warned, since no messenger had come to them for a long period.

Fahum ghāfilūn: That is, they do not know the outcome of the disbelief and misguidance they are in, nor do they recognise what would save them from it, which is faith and righteous deeds.

Laqad ḥaqqa al-qawlu ʿalā aktharihim: That is, the punishment became due for most of them, and therefore they do not believe.

Innā jaʿalnā fī aʿnāqihim aghlālan: That is, We made their hands fastened to their necks with shackles.

Fahiya ilā al-adhqān: That is, their hands are gathered up to their chins. Al-adhqān is the plural of dhaqan, which is the junction of the two jaws.

Fahum muqmaḥūn: That is, they have their heads raised, unable to lower them, and therefore they do not spend their hands on good, nor do they humble their heads to accept the truth.

Fa-aghshaynāhum fahum lā yubṣirūn: That is, We placed a covering over their sight, and therefore they do not see.

Wa-sawāʾun ʿalayhimaʾandhartahum am lam tundhirhum lā yuʾminūn: That is, your warning to them and your not warning them are equal in their failure to believe.

Man ittaba al-dhikr: That is, the Qur'an.

Wa-ajrun karīm: That is, with Paradise, the abode of bliss and peace.

Innā naḥnu nuḥyī al-mawtā: That is, We, the Lord of Might, give life to the dead for resurrection and recompense.

Wa-naktubu mā qaddamū wa-āthārahum: That is, what they did of good and evil during their lives, so that We may reckon with them; and their traces (āthār), that is, their steps to the mosques and whatever any person after them has initiated.

Fī imāmin mubīn: That is, in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūz).

Meaning of the verses:

﴿Yā Sīn﴾ Allah knows best what He intends by it. ﴿Wal-Qur'ān al-Ḥakīm﴾, that is, the firmly structured in arrangement and meaning, and the possessor of wisdom who places everything in its proper place. The Exalted swore by the wise Qur'an that Muhammad ﷺ is a prophet and messenger, saying: ﴿Wal-Qur'ān al-Ḥakīm. Innaka lamina al-mursalīn ʿalā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm﴾, which is Islam. His saying ﴿Tanzīla al-ʿazīzi al-raḥīm﴾ means this Qur'an is the revelation of Allah, ﴿al-ʿazīz﴾ in retribution against those who disbelieve in it and deny His messenger, ﴿al-raḥīm﴾ toward His friends and righteous servants. His saying ﴿Li-tundhira qawman mā unndhira ābāʾuhum﴾ means: We sent you and revealed the Book to you so that you might warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, being the idolaters of the Arabs, since no messenger had come to them after Ismāʿīl (ʿalayhi al-salām). ﴿Fahum ghāfilūn﴾ means they do not know the outcome of their idolatry, evil and corruption. To warn them (tundhiruhum) means to frighten them with the punishment of Allah that follows idolatry and sins.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Laqad ḥaqqa al-qawlu ʿalā aktharihim﴾ means: upon most of the opponents of the Prophet ﷺ, from the disbelievers of Quraysh such as Abū Jahl, the word became due, which is His saying ﴿La-amla'anna jahannama mina al-jinnati wa-al-nāsi ajmaʿīn﴾ [Hud 11:119; al-Sajda 32:13], so punishment became due for them, and therefore they do not believe; for had they believed they would not have been punished. Their non-belief was not imposed upon them; it was by their choice and freedom of will, for had it been compulsion they would not have deserved punishment for it. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Innā jaʿalnā fī aʿnāqihim aghlālan fahiya﴾, that is, their hands, ﴿ilā al-adhqān﴾, are fastened with shackles, ﴿fahum muqmaḥūn﴾, that is, raising their heads and unable to lower them. This is an illustration of their state: they do not extend their hands to spend in good, and their heads do not submit to accept the truth. His saying ﴿Wa-jaʿalnā min bayni aydīhim saddan wa-min khalfihim saddan﴾ is another illustration of their state: the life of this world was made attractive to them, so they see nothing beyond it; this is a barrier before them preventing them from faith and from abandoning idolatry and sins; and the Hereafter was depicted to them in a false form, impossible to occur, and that was a barrier behind them. Therefore they do not repent nor remember, because they do not fear the punishment of the Hereafter. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Fa-aghshaynāhum﴾ is an intensification of their misguidance: He placed over their eyes a covering because of their hatred of the Messenger ﷺ and their detestation of what he brought, so they are blind and do not see. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Wa-sawāʾun ʿalayhim aʾandhartahum am lam tundhirhum lā yuʾminūn﴾ is information from Him, Exalted is He, that this group of the Messenger's ﷺ opponents, the greatest criminals of Mecca, are equal in regard to the prophetic warning and its absence, so they do not believe. It is as if Allah said to His Messenger: these obstinate opponents of yours, your warning does not benefit them; so warn those whom your warning benefits and leave others, which is His saying ﴿Innamā tundhiru man ittaba al-dhikr﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿wa-khashiya al-Raḥmāna bil-ghayb﴾, that is, he feared Him and did not disobey Him, though he did not see Him, just as he did not disobey Him when alone with himself where no one else could see. Such a person is given the good news of forgiveness from Us for his sins and a generous reward for his righteous deeds, which is Paradise, the abode of the God-fearing. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Innā naḥnu nuḥyī al-mawtā﴾, that is, for resurrection and recompense; ﴿wa-naktubu mā qaddamū﴾, that is, those dead during their lifetimes, of good and evil; ﴿wa-āthārahum﴾, that is, and We record their traces, which are what was initiated of their good or evil practices. ﴿Wa-kulla shayʾin﴾, that is, of acts of worship and others, ﴿fī imāmin mubīn﴾, which is the Preserved Tablet, and We will recompense each according to what he did. In this address there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of Muhammad's prophethood and confirmation of his mission ﷺ.

2- Explanation of the wisdom behind sending the Messenger and revealing the noble Book.

3- Explanation that the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ was sent during a gap between messengers.

4- Explanation that love of this world, devotion to it, and neglect of the Hereafter and not turning to it place a person between two barriers which he cannot pass or free himself from.

5- Explanation that sins bind their doer and come between him and doing good or accepting the truth.

6- Explanation that whoever initiates a good or bad practice that is followed after him is recompensed for it, just as he is recompensed for the deed he performed with his own hand.

7- Affirmation of the doctrine of divine decree and predestination, and that everything is in the Book of Decrees, referred to as the Imam. The meaning of "mubīn" is that what is written therein is clear and manifest, nothing from it being unknown.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 13–19:

Explanation of the words:

﴿وَاضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا﴾: that is, make for them an example (mathal).

Ashab al-qarya (the people of the town): that is Antakya, the capital of Bilad al-Iqrah (also called al-Awasim), in the land of the Romans (al-Rum).

Idh ja'aha al-mursalun (when the messengers came to it): that is, the messengers of ʿIsa (peace be upon him).

Fa-ʿazzazna bi-thalith (then We strengthened [them] with a third): that is, We strengthened the matter of the two messengers and their call with a third messenger, who was Habib ibn al-Najjar.

Wa-ma ʿalayna illa al-balagh al-mubin (and upon us is only the clear conveyance): that is, the plain and evident conveyance, with clear proofs, which were the healing of the blind, the leper, and the sick, and the raising of the dead.

Inna tatayyarna bikum (indeed we see an omen in you): that is, we consider you a bad omen, because the rain has been withheld from us on account of you.

Qalu ta'irukum maʿakum (they said: your omen is with you): that is, your ill omen is with you, and it is your disbelief in your Lord.

A-in dhukkirtum (what, when you are admonished): that is, when you are advised and warned, you take it as an omen. This is a rebuke to them.

Bal antum qawm musrifun (nay, you are a people who exceed [all bounds]): that is, you transgress the limit in polytheism and disbelief.

Explanation of the meaning of the verses:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And present to them an example﴾: that is, present, O Messenger, to your people, who are insistent upon polytheism and in denying you and the guidance and the religion of truth you brought them, ﴿an example: the people of the town﴾, for their state in denial and extremism in disbelief and obstinacy is like the state of these people. ﴿When the messengers came to it﴾, and they were the messengers of ʿIsa (peace be upon him), when he sent two messengers. Then, when they harmed the two with beating and imprisonment, he sent Shamʿun al-Safi, the chief of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun), to strengthen their position, as the Exalted said: ﴿So they denied them, and We strengthened [them] with a third﴾. They said to the people of Antakya: ﴿Indeed, we have been sent to you﴾ from ʿIsa (peace be upon him), calling you to worship the Most Merciful and to abandon the worship of idols. ﴿They said: You are not but humans like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are only lying﴾: that is, you are only lying against us in your claim that you are messengers to us. The messengers said: ﴿Our Lord knows that we are indeed sent to you﴾. So they confronted the people's doubt about them with what removes doubt: the oath and the emphasis of the statement by the nominal sentence and the emphatic lam. So they said: ﴿Our Lord knows that we are indeed sent to you, and upon us is only the clear conveyance﴾: that is, the plain and evident [conveyance]. If you accept what we call you to, that is your share of good and salvation; and if you refuse, that is your share of destruction and loss. The people of Antakya replied to the messengers, saying: ﴿Indeed, we see an omen in you﴾: that is, we consider you a bad omen, since the rain has been withheld from us on account of you. The messengers answered them with their saying: ﴿Your omen is with you﴾: that is, your ill omen lies in your disbelief and your denial; that is why God has withheld the rain from you. Then they said to them, rebuking them: ﴿What, when you are admonished?﴾: that is, when you are advised and warned by God, that you may be righteous, you take it as an omen. Nay, you, O people, are ﴿a people who exceed [all bounds]﴾: that is, you transgress the limit in disbelief, polytheism and aggression.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The recommendation of giving an example, which is depicting a strange state by another similar state, as here in the story of Habib ibn al-Najjar.

2- The similarity of the condition of the disbelievers in denial and persistence in every time and place.

3- The resort of the people of disbelief, after the proof has been established against them, to threat and intimidation.

4- The prohibition of tatayyur (taking omens) and tashaʾum (considering something ill-omened) in Islam.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 20–27:

Explanation of the words:

"And there came a man": that is, Habib ibn al-Najjar, the companion of Ya-Sin.

"From the farthest part of the city": that is, from the farthest of the city's quarters, and it was Antioch, the capital.

"Running": that is, hurrying with great speed, when news reached him that the people of the town had resolved to kill the three messengers of Jesus.

"He said: O my people, follow the messengers": that is, the messengers of Jesus, upon him be peace.

"Follow those who ask no reward of you": that is, follow those who do not ask you for any payment for conveying the call to the truth.

"And they are guided": that is, the messengers are upon guidance from their Lord, and they are not liars.

"Who created me" (fatarani): that is, who brought me into being.

"If the Most Merciful should intend me harm" (bi-durr): that is, with sickness or the like.

"Nor can they save me" (wa la yunqidhun): that is, from what God has willed for me of harm to my body or otherwise.

"Then indeed I would be in clear error": that is, if I were to take gods besides God and worship them, I would indeed be in clear error.

"Indeed I have believed in your Lord, so hear me": that is, he declared this statement openly to his people, and they killed him.

"It was said: Enter Paradise": the angels said to him at death, "Enter Paradise."

"Would that my people knew": he said this when he witnessed his station in Paradise.

"Of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honoured": that is, faith, monotheism, and patience upon these.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the parable of the people of the town. After the position of the three messengers was strengthened, and God granted them marvels by which they healed the sick and even revived the dead by God's permission, and they gained believing followers, the rulers of the land grew angry and wished to seize the messengers by force. This reached Habib ibn al-Najjar, who was an elderly believing monotheist living at the farthest edge of the city, so he came running on foot, commanded and forbade, and openly declared his faith and monotheism to the people, and they killed him by trampling him with their feet. God the Exalted said: "And there came from the farthest part of the city" – Antioch – "a man running," that is, walking swiftly, when news reached him that the people of the land had resolved to kill the three messengers. And as soon as he reached the raging crowd, he cried out with the loudest voice: "O my people, follow the messengers." He asked the messengers whether they had demanded any reward for conveying the call of Jesus, and they said no. So he said: "Follow those who ask no reward of you, and they are guided," so follow them and you will be guided by their guidance. The people said to him: "Are you worshipping God like them, and not worshipping our gods?" He said: "And why should I not worship He who created me," that is, what would prevent me from worshipping Him when He created me, "and to Him you will be returned," that is, after your death, when He will call you to account and recompense you for your deeds. Then he seized the opportunity to call to his Lord, saying in the form of a question: "Shall I take besides Him gods," that is, idols and images that neither hear nor see, "If the Most Merciful should intend me harm, their intercession will avail me nothing at all," even slightly, "nor can they save me," from what He intends for me of harm or the like. "Indeed, then I would be in clear error," that is, if I worship these idols that neither benefit nor harm, I would be in clear error, manifest and evident, needing no proof. Then he raised his voice, announcing: "Indeed I have believed in your Lord," that is, your Creator, your Provider, and the Owner of your affairs, apart from these idols and images, "so hear me." At this they rushed upon him and killed him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 20–27:

Explanation of the words:

"And there came a man": that is, Habib ibn al-Najjar, the companion of Ya-Sin.

"From the farthest part of the city": that is, from the farthest of the city's quarters, and it was Antioch, the capital.

"Running": that is, hurrying with great speed, when news reached him that the people of the town had resolved to kill the three messengers of Jesus.

"He said: O my people, follow the messengers": that is, the messengers of Jesus, upon him be peace.

"Follow those who ask no reward of you": that is, follow those who do not ask you for any payment for conveying the call to the truth.

"And they are guided": that is, the messengers are upon guidance from their Lord, and they are not liars.

"Who created me" (fatarani): that is, who brought me into being.

"If the Most Merciful should intend me harm" (bi-durr): that is, with sickness or the like.

"Nor can they save me" (wa la yunqidhun): that is, from what God has willed for me of harm to my body or otherwise.

"Then indeed I would be in clear error": that is, if I were to take gods besides God and worship them, I would indeed be in clear error.

"Indeed I have believed in your Lord, so hear me": that is, he declared this statement openly to his people, and they killed him.

"It was said: Enter Paradise": the angels said to him at death, "Enter Paradise."

"Would that my people knew": he said this when he witnessed his station in Paradise.

"Of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honoured": that is, faith, monotheism, and patience upon these.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the parable of the people of the town. After the position of the three messengers was strengthened, and God granted them marvels by which they healed the sick and even revived the dead by God's permission, and they gained believing followers, the rulers of the land grew angry and wished to seize the messengers by force. This reached Habib ibn al-Najjar, who was an elderly believing monotheist living at the farthest edge of the city, so he came running on foot, commanded and forbade, and openly declared his faith and monotheism to the people, and they killed him by trampling him with their feet. God the Exalted said: "And there came from the farthest part of the city" – Antioch – "a man running," that is, walking swiftly, when news reached him that the people of the land had resolved to kill the three messengers. And as soon as he reached the raging crowd, he cried out with the loudest voice: "O my people, follow the messengers." He asked the messengers whether they had demanded any reward for conveying the call of Jesus, and they said no. So he said: "Follow those who ask no reward of you, and they are guided," so follow them and you will be guided by their guidance. The people said to him: "Are you worshipping God like them, and not worshipping our gods?" He said: "And why should I not worship He who created me," that is, what would prevent me from worshipping Him when He created me, "and to Him you will be returned," that is, after your death, when He will call you to account and recompense you for your deeds. Then he seized the opportunity to call to his Lord, saying in the form of a question: "Shall I take besides Him gods," that is, idols and images that neither hear nor see, "If the Most Merciful should intend me harm, their intercession will avail me nothing at all," even slightly, "nor can they save me," from what He intends for me of harm or the like. "Indeed, then I would be in clear error," that is, if I worship these idols that neither benefit nor harm, I would be in clear error, manifest and evident, needing no proof. Then he raised his voice, announcing: "Indeed I have believed in your Lord," that is, your Creator, your Provider, and the Owner of your affairs, apart from these idols and images, "so hear me." At this they rushed upon him and killed him.

When it was said to him, "Enter Paradise," and he saw its bliss, he remembered his people, advising them, saying: "Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honoured." That is, that they might know what He forgave him and made him among the honoured, namely faith and monotheism, so that they would believe and affirm the Oneness of God. Thus he advised his people while alive and dead, and this is the way of the Muslim of good Islam and the sincere believer of true faith: he advises and does not deceive, guides and does not mislead, however they speak to him and whatever harshness and cruelty they treat him with, even unto death by killing.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Demonstration of the honour of Habib ibn al-Najjar, who advised his people while alive and dead.

2- Demonstration of what the adherents of monotheism and the true religion encounter in every time and place of hardships and terrors.

3- The obligation to convey the call to truth and to denounce polytheism, however severe the punishment.

4- The good news for the believer at death, especially the martyr, for he sees Paradise with his own eyes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verse 28–32:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven﴾: i.e., upon the people of Habib ibn al-Najjar, who were the people of Antioch.

"After him": i.e., after his death.

"Any host from the heaven": i.e., angels, to destroy them.

"And We are not ones who send down": i.e., the angels were not sent down to destroy the nations that deserved destruction.

"It was but one Cry": i.e., it was only one Cry, the Cry of Jibril (peace be upon him).

"Then behold, they were extinguished": i.e., silent, motionless, dead.

"Alas for the servants!": i.e., O regret of the servants, this is your time to appear, so appear. This is the utmost of anguish. The "servants" are those who denied the messengers and disbelieved in the Oneness of God.

"Never came to them a messenger but they used to mock him": this is the cause of the regret over them.

"Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them?": i.e., have not the people of Makkah, who denied the Messenger ﷺ, seen?

"And all of them, all of them, will surely be brought before Us": i.e., all creatures, without exception, will be brought before Us on the Day of Resurrection for their reckoning and recompense.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted said, ﴿And We did not send down upon his people﴾, i.e., the people of Habib ibn al-Najjar, ﴿after him﴾, i.e., after his death, ﴿any host from the heaven﴾ to take vengeance on his people who killed him, because he denounced their polytheism and called them to Oneness, ﴿and We are not ones who send down﴾, since there was no need that called for it. ﴿It was but one Cry from Jibril (peace be upon him), and then behold, they were extinguished﴾, i.e., destroyed, silent, dead, without motion, without life in them. And His saying, ﴿Alas for the servants!﴾, i.e., O regret of the servants over themselves; appear, O regret, this is your time to appear. ﴿Never came to them a messenger but they used to mock him﴾: this is the cause and requirement of the regret, namely their mockery of the messengers. And His saying, ﴿Have they not seen﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾, i.e., did they not know of the many generations We destroyed before them, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and the companions of Madyan, ﴿that they do not return to them﴾. This should have been a guide and admonition for them, so that they would believe, affirm the Oneness of God, be saved from punishment and be happy. And His saying, ﴿And all of them﴾, i.e., of the destroyed nations and of all other servants, ﴿all of them will surely be brought before Us﴾, i.e., they will all be brought before Us for the decisive judgment on the Day of Resurrection, whereupon the believers will be saved and the disbelievers will perish.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Manifestations of God's power in destroying the people of Antioch with a single Cry.

2- Expressing regret over the servants for themselves, since they are the wrongdoers who denied; the regret is from them and upon them.

3- The prohibition of mocking what is among the sacred things of God which must be venerated.

4- Seeking a lesson from the reports and conditions of those who came before, and the wise is one who takes a lesson from others.

5- Affirmation of the Return, the Reckoning and the Recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 33–36:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth⦆: that is, as evidence for the truth of the resurrection and its certain occurrence.

"We have revived it": by sending down rain upon it, so that it becomes living with plants and crops.

"And We made therein gardens": that is, orchards.

"And what their hands made": that is, their hands did not make it; it is rather the creation and making of Allah.

"Will they not then be grateful?": that is, do they see these blessings and yet not thank for them? This is a disgraceful stance on their part.

"Glory be to He who created all the pairs": that is, exalted and sanctified is Allah, who created all the kinds.

"And of themselves": that is, males and females.

"And of that which they do not know": of the creatures such as those in the heavens and beneath the earths.

Meaning of the verses:

Since the preceding verses established the doctrine of resurrection and recompense in His saying, "And all of them will be brought before Us" (Ya-Sin 36:32), here He mentions the rational proof of the possibility of resurrection, saying, ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth⦆ — that is, as evidence of the truth of the resurrection: the earth that has been struck by barrenness, with no plant or crop in it, which We revive with rain, so that it brings forth every beautiful pair. This is a sign, that is, a great proof and a clear argument for the possibility of resurrection, since the creatures die and nothing remains but Allah the Exalted: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish, but there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor⦆ (Ar-Rahman 55:26–27). Then Allah the Exalted sends down water from beneath the Throne, and mankind lives in the same manner as the dead earth, upon which rain is sent down and it lives by plants. And this time it lives by humans, for their creation is assembled from a bone called the "coccyx" (ʿajb al-dhanab), which is in the belly of the earth and does not decay, and from which creation is assembled, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed us in the Sahih. This is the meaning of His saying, in argument for the resurrection: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth; We have revived it and brought forth from it grain⦆, that is, wheat grain, from which they eat bread. And His saying ﴿And We made therein⦆, that is, in the dead earth, gardens — that is, orchards of palm trees and grapevines — ﴿and caused springs to gush forth in it⦆, that is, springs of water. These are manifestations of divine power and knowledge, and all of them testify to the truth of the resurrection, its possibility, and that Allah the Exalted is capable of it and of its like. His saying, ﴿that they may eat of its fruit⦆, that is, of the fruit of what was mentioned, of the palm and the grape and other things. His saying, ﴿and their hands did not make it⦆, that is, their hands did not create it nor bring it into being; rather, the hand of Allah is what created it. ﴿Will they not then be grateful?⦆ He rebukes them for their failure to thank Him for the blessing of sustenance He has bestowed upon them. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs⦆, that is, exalted and sanctified is Allah, who created all the pairs ﴿of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of that which they do not know⦆. He, Exalted is He, glorifies and exalts Himself, declaring Himself free of inability to re-create, and reminds of the signs of power and knowledge, which is the system of pairing, since all creatures are pairs, that is, kinds of male and female. Plants, in all their variety, are male and female, and so are people; and what is hidden from us in the heavens and in the belly of the earth is likewise in pairs. And there is no single one (witr), that is, no unique being except Allah the Exalted, who is transcendent above the attributes of creatures. From this pairing there is, for the life of this world, another kind that corresponds to it, like a spouse, and that is the life to come. This is a rational proof, among the strongest proofs of the second life.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The establishment of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, which is the driving force for a person to do good and abstain from evils and wrongful deeds.

2- The proof of the system of pairing, which is a sign that the Qur'an is the revelation and speech of Allah, since the Qur'an established the system of pairing before people knew of this system in the atom and elsewhere in the twentieth century.

3- The obligation to thank Allah the Exalted through faith and obedience to Him and to His Messenger for His blessings, among them the blessing of creation and the blessing of sustenance, that is, through food, water, and air.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 37–40:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness.﴾ (wa-ayatun lahum al-layl naslakh minhu al-nahar): a sign for them of the possibility of resurrection. We remove the day from the night, so that they are in darkness.

﴿To a resting place for it.﴾ (li-mustaqarr lahā): a place for it that it does not exceed.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ (dhalika taqdir al-'Azīz al-'Alīm): its running in its orbit is a decree, that is, its ordering by the Almighty in His dominion, the All-Knowing of all His creation.

﴿And the moon, We have measured for it stations.﴾ (wa-al-qamar qaddarnāhu manāzil): another sign, which is the measuring of the moon's stations, which are twenty-eight stations.

﴿Until it returns like the old date-stalk.﴾ (ḥattā ʿāda ka-al-ʿurjūn al-qadīm): that is, until it returns like the stalk of a date cluster, whose base is on the palm tree and whose tip is at the strands, yellow, thin, and curved, like the moon when it is at the end of the month.

﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon.﴾ (lā al-shams yanbaghī lahā an tudrika al-qamar): it is not proper for the sun, nor easy for it, to overtake the moon so that they would meet at night.

﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day.﴾ (wa-lā al-layl sābiq al-nahār): that is, by coming before its end.

﴿And each in an orbit is swimming.﴾ (wa-kull fī falak yasbaḥūn): that is, each of the sun, the moon and the wandering stars is swimming, that is, moving, in an orbit. The falak (orbit, from the technical term falak, meaning the circular path) is a round circle like the spindle's whorl, and it is the course of the two luminaries and the wandering planets.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to demonstrate the possibility of resurrection and its certain occurrence. Almighty God says: ﴿And a sign⦆ that is, another sign for them of God's power over resurrection: ﴿the night, We strip from it the day⦆ that is, We separate the day from it, meaning We remove it from it, so that they are in darkness, that is, entering into darkness. This is a sign of God's power over resurrection. His saying ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it⦆ means it runs in its orbit; from it begins its course and to it its course ends, and that is its resting place. It has another resting place, which is the end of the worldly life. Indeed it prostrates every day beneath the Throne and asks permission to resume its circling, and permission is granted to it, as the report has been authentically transmitted from the master of mankind, Muhammad (ﷺ). Its being beneath the Throne is no strange matter, for the whole universe is beneath the Throne. Its asking permission and being granted it is no strange matter either, since the ant manages its life by the permission of its Lord, speaks, thinks and works; the sun is more deserving of this, and it speaks in its own particular speech, asks permission, and permission is given to it. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty⦆ that is, the Dominant over His will, the All-Knowing of all His creation. The decree of the sun's course in its orbit, in which it traverses millions of miles in a second, is a wondrous matter, and the order of its course throughout life is not disturbed by a minute, nor does its level rise or fall by a hand's breadth, for that would entail the ruin of the earthly world. All of this none can bring about but God. Is not the Originator of this originating in creation and governance able to bring to life those He created and to cause them to die? Yes, indeed, truly God is capable of all things. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And the moon, We have measured for it stations until it returns like the old date-stalk⦆ is another sign of the possibility of resurrection and its inevitability. The moon is a luminous body that revolves around the earth, moving through its twenty-eight stations with extraordinary precision and exact reckoning, so that the inhabitants of the earth may thereby know the number of years and reckoning; for were it not for it, no day, week, month, year or century would be known. The moon begins as a small crescent and starts to appear, growing a little with its appearing, bit by bit, until at the middle of the month it becomes a full moon. Then it begins to wane and dwindle in a wondrous order, until at the end of the month it becomes like the old date-stalk, that is, like the stalk of the date cluster: yellow, thin, and curved. All of this is for the benefit of the human being who lives on the surface of this earth. Is this not a great sign of the power of the Almighty, the All-Knowing, to restore life for the wisdom of reckoning and recompense? Yes, indeed it is a great sign. His saying ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon⦆ means it is not easy for the sun, nor proper for it, to overtake the moon so that its light would be extinguished; rather each has its own course, so they meet only rarely at a particular part of the horizon, whence occur the lunar eclipse and the solar eclipse. His saying ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day⦆ rather, each of the night and the day runs on a drawn line that it does not exceed; therefore the night does not outstrip the day nor the day the night, and they do not mingle except by a part of one entering the other, and a part of the other entering the first, which is the meaning of ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night⦆ [al-Hadid: 6]. His saying ﴿And each in an orbit is swimming⦆ means each one of the sun, the moon and the wandering stars is swimming in an orbit; therefore no confusion occurs among them, nor does any of them collide with another, until the end of life, when that occurs and the universe is ruined.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The establishment of decisive proofs and clear demonstrations of the possibility of resurrection and its certain occurrence.

2- The Qur'an's mention of matters of the heavenly spheres, of which people today know only a small part, is a great sign that it is the revelation of God, and that the one to whom it was revealed is certainly the Messenger of God.

3- What the Qur'an says about the upper cosmos is so clear that a farmer and a shepherd know it as well as the learned scholar and the unlettered man who neither reads nor writes, so that the proof may be established against people if they do not believe in God, do not single Him out in worship, and do not devote themselves to obeying Him and obeying His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 37–40:

﴿To a resting place for it.﴾ (li-mustaqarr lahā): a place for it that it does not exceed.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ (dhalika taqdir al-'Azīz al-'Alīm): its running in its orbit is a decree, that is, its ordering by the Almighty in His dominion, the All-Knowing of all His creation.

﴿And the moon, We have measured for it stations.﴾ (wa-al-qamar qaddarnāhu manāzil): another sign, which is the measuring of the moon's stations, which are twenty-eight stations.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 41–46:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And a sign for them﴾: that is, a sign for them of Our power to resurrect.

﴿That We carried their offspring﴾: that is, the descendants of the people of Noah whom We destroyed by the flood. We saved their descendants because they were believers who affirmed the oneness of God, and We drowned their fathers because they were polytheists.

﴿In the laden ship﴾: that is, in the ship of Noah, filled with pairs of every kind.

﴿And We created for them the like thereof﴾: that is, of the like of Noah's ship, that they ride.

﴿Then there is no one to cry out for them﴾: that is, no helper to save them, so their cries are not answered.

﴿And as provision for a while﴾: that is, and as a provision for them of food and drink until the end of their appointed terms.

﴿Beware of what is before you﴾: that is, of the punishment of this world, by faith and steadfastness.

﴿And what is behind you﴾: that is, of the punishment of the Hereafter, if you persist in disbelief and denial.

﴿And there does not come to them any sign﴾: that is, and there does not come to them any sign or any proof from the proofs of the Qur'an and any clear evidence from its evidences, indicating the oneness of God and the truthfulness of the Messenger, except that they turn away from it, neither heeding it nor caring for it.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues presenting cosmic signs to demonstrate resurrection, oneness and prophethood. God the Exalted says: ﴿And a sign for them﴾, that is, another sign besides what preceded it: ﴿that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾. That is, We carried the descendants of the believing people of Noah and saved them for their faith and their affirmation of God's oneness, and We drowned the polytheists. This is a clear sign of God's approval of the believing monotheists and His wrath against the disbelieving, polytheistic, denying ones. In this salvation of the monotheists and drowning of the polytheists is a sign and a lesson, if the polytheists of Quraysh in Mecca would understand. And God's words: ﴿And We created for them the like thereof that they ride﴾. This is another sign as well: God saved the monotheists in an ark that had no precedent, then created for them its like, which they ride until the Day of Resurrection. Had He willed to cancel that, they would have had no ship until the Day of Resurrection. Another sign: ﴿And if We will, We drown them, then there is no one to cry out for them﴾, which is His power to drown the disbelieving riders of ships; if We did so, they would find no one to cry out or to help them and save them from drowning. ﴿Except as a mercy from Us﴾: except Our mercy, which reaches them and saves them, so that they enjoy in their lives what they used to enjoy until the time of their appointed terms arrives. And God's words: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, that perhaps you may receive mercy"﴾: that is, when it is said to these deniers of God's signs, who turn away from His religion and associate others with Him: beware of the punishment before you, where its cause is present, which is your disbelief and obstinacy, and of the punishment of the Hereafter behind you, where its requirement exists, which is polytheism and denial, in hope that you may be shown mercy and not be punished, they turned away as though they had not heard. And His words: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs﴾ of their Lord's speech, the noble Qur'an, bearing proofs and evidences for the truth of what it calls to of faith and monotheism, except that they turn away from it completely, as though their hearts were hewn from stone, and God the Exalted is our refuge.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. The demonstration of God's favor upon humanity in saving the descendants of the disbelieving people of Noah, for from them came mankind; otherwise, had God drowned all of them, the believing descendants and the disbelieving fathers alike, no one would have remained on earth.

2. God's protection of His servants and His care for them; otherwise they would all have perished. But where is their gratitude?

3. The demonstration of the persistence and obstinacy of the disbelievers of Quraysh, a matter without precedent.

4. The indication, by the word "like" in His words ﴿of the like thereof﴾, to the variety of ships, from battleships and submarines to torpedo boats.

1. The demonstration of God's favor upon humanity in saving the descendants of the disbelieving people of Noah, for from them came mankind; otherwise, had God drowned all of them, the believing descendants and the disbelieving fathers alike, no one would have remained on earth.

2. God's protection of His servants and His care for them; otherwise they would all have perished. But where is their gratitude?

3. The demonstration of the persistence and obstinacy of the disbelievers of Quraysh, a matter without precedent.

4. The indication, by the word "like" in His words ﴿of the like thereof﴾, to the variety of ships, from battleships and submarines to torpedo boats.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 41–46:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And a sign for them﴾: that is, a sign for them of Our power to resurrect.

﴿That We carried their offspring﴾: that is, the descendants of the people of Noah whom We destroyed by the flood. We saved their descendants because they were believers who affirmed the oneness of God, and We drowned their fathers because they were polytheists.

﴿In the laden ship﴾: that is, in the ship of Noah, filled with pairs of every kind.

﴿And We created for them the like thereof﴾: that is, of the like of Noah's ship, that they ride.

﴿Then there is no one to cry out for them﴾: that is, no helper to save them, so their cries are not answered.

﴿And as provision for a while﴾: that is, and as a provision for them of food and drink until the end of their appointed terms.

﴿Beware of what is before you﴾: that is, of the punishment of this world, by faith and steadfastness.

﴿And what is behind you﴾: that is, of the punishment of the Hereafter, if you persist in disbelief and denial.

﴿And there does not come to them any sign﴾: that is, and there does not come to them any sign or any proof from the proofs of the Qur'an and any clear evidence from its evidences, indicating the oneness of God and the truthfulness of the Messenger, except that they turn away from it, neither heeding it nor caring for it.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues presenting cosmic signs to demonstrate resurrection, oneness and prophethood. God the Exalted says: ﴿And a sign for them﴾, that is, another sign besides what preceded it: ﴿that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾. That is, We carried the descendants of the believing people of Noah and saved them for their faith and their affirmation of God's oneness, and We drowned the polytheists. This is a clear sign of God's approval of the believing monotheists and His wrath against the disbelieving, polytheistic, denying ones. In this salvation of the monotheists and drowning of the polytheists is a sign and a lesson, if the polytheists of Quraysh in Mecca would understand. And God's words: ﴿And We created for them the like thereof that they ride﴾. This is another sign as well: God saved the monotheists in an ark that had no precedent, then created for them its like, which they ride until the Day of Resurrection. Had He willed to cancel that, they would have had no ship until the Day of Resurrection. Another sign: ﴿And if We will, We drown them, then there is no one to cry out for them﴾, which is His power to drown the disbelieving riders of ships; if We did so, they would find no one to cry out or to help them and save them from drowning. ﴿Except as a mercy from Us﴾: except Our mercy, which reaches them and saves them, so that they enjoy in their lives what they used to enjoy until the time of their appointed terms arrives. And God's words: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, that perhaps you may receive mercy"﴾: that is, when it is said to these deniers of God's signs, who turn away from His religion and associate others with Him: beware of the punishment before you, where its cause is present, which is your disbelief and obstinacy, and of the punishment of the Hereafter behind you, where its requirement exists, which is polytheism and denial, in hope that you may be shown mercy and not be punished, they turned away as though they had not heard. And His words: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs﴾ of their Lord's speech, the noble Qur'an, bearing proofs and evidences for the truth of what it calls to of faith and monotheism, except that they turn away from it completely, as though their hearts were hewn from stone, and God the Exalted is our refuge.

Explanation of the words:

"And when it is said to them, 'Spend of what Allah has provided you': that is, when the poor believers in Makkah say to the disbelieving wealthy, 'Spend on us.'"

"Of what Allah has provided you": that is, of wealth.

"Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?": that is, they said to the believers, mocking them, "Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?"

"You are not but in clear error": that is, you poor ones are not but in clear error in your belief which you hold.

"When is this promise": that is, the final resurrection, if you are truthful about it.

"They await not but a single shout": that is, they await nothing but a single shout, which is the blast of Israfil.

"It will seize them while they are disputing": that is, the Shout will seize them while they are quarrelling over buying and selling, eating and drinking, for it will come upon them suddenly while they are unaware.

"And they will not be able to make a bequest": that is, none of them will be able to make a will.

"Nor will they return to their people": rather, they will perish where they are, in their markets, farms, factories, cafés or places of amusement.

"And when they are sent forth from the graves to their Lord, hastening": that is, from the graves, hastening (yansiluna), that is, they will come out quickly.

"They will say, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?'": that is, the disbelievers say, "Who has raised us from our graves?"

"This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers told the truth": that is, this is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth in what they reported.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And when it is said to them﴾: that is, when it is said to those polytheistic, denying, heretical disbelievers, and those who say it are the believers. It is narrated that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq used to feed the needy Muslims, and Abu Jahl met him and said, "O Abu Bakr, do you claim that Allah is able to feed these people?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then why does He not feed them?" He said, "He tests some people with poverty and some with wealth, and commands the poor to be patient and commands the rich to give." Abu Jahl said, "By Allah, O Abu Bakr, you are only in clear error. Do you claim that Allah is able to feed these people, yet He does not feed them, and then you feed them?" So this verse was revealed. And with this narration the meaning of the noble verse becomes clear: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾, that is, to the disbelievers, ﴿Spend of what Allah has provided you﴾ upon the needy, ﴿those who disbelieved said to those who believed﴾, those who were commanding them to spend, ﴿Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?﴾ They said this mockingly and in disbelief. ﴿You are not﴾, that is, you Muslims, ﴿but in clear error﴾, that is, but in a departure from the truth and a deviation from right guidance, clear to whoever reflects and contemplates it.

His saying, ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"﴾: that is, those heretical deniers of the resurrection say, mockingly and impatiently, "When is this promise which you promise us, O Muslims, if you are truthful in your claim?"

He, the Exalted, said, ﴿They await not but a single shout﴾, which is the blast of Israfil on the Horn, the blast of annihilation, ﴿that will seize them while they are disputing﴾, that is, they will be quarrelling in their markets, buying and selling, and in their public and private gatherings, when it comes upon them suddenly while they are unaware. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest﴾, which one of them could make to his son or brother, ﴿nor to their families will they return﴾, that is, to their homes, their wives and their children, but they will fall unconscious where they are.

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾, that is, the Horn of Israfil, which is a trumpet, also called the bugle, the blast of resurrection from the graves, alive. ﴿And behold, from the graves﴾, the plural of jadath, which is the grave, ﴿they will hasten﴾, that is, walking swiftly, toward their Lord for the decisive judgment and ruling between them concerning what they differed about in this world, of faith and disbelief, goodness and evil, justice and injustice. ﴿They will say, "Woe to us!"﴾, that is, they call out for their own woe and destruction, because of what they witness of the terrors of the standing place. ﴿Who has raised us from our sleeping place?﴾ And the believers answered them with their saying, ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers told the truth﴾, since Allah promised us His meeting and the messengers informed us of it and of its details.

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿It will not be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾, that is, it will be only one shout from Israfil, and at once all of them will stand before Allah, the Exalted, to be reckoned and recompensed. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in anything﴾, that is, on this day when creation stands before its Lord, no soul will be wronged in anything, neither by a reduction of its good deeds nor by an increase in its bad deeds, and you, O servants, will not be recompensed except for what you used to do, of good and evil.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Demonstration of the arrogance, tyranny, mockery and ridicule of the disbelievers, because of the darkness of disbelief upon their hearts.

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mentioning its beginnings and its ends.

3- The Hour will come only suddenly.

4- The cosmic upheaval which occurs, due to its magnitude, scholars differ in determining the blasts in it, and the apparent view is that they are four: the first is the blast of annihilation, the second is the blast of resurrection, the third is the blast of terror and swooning, and the fourth is the blast of standing before the Lord of the worlds.

5- Affirmation of divine justice on the Day of Reckoning and Recompense, so that every doer may be reassured that he will be repaid for his deeds and no more.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 55–58:

Explanation of the words:

﴿In busy occupation, they will be joyful﴾: That is, the people of Paradise will be occupied with something other than what the people of the Fire suffer of punishment and misery. Their preoccupation, which absorbs them, is the lasting bliss in the Abode of Peace.

﴿Joyful﴾: That is, enjoying themselves in delight with blessings, owing to the goodness of their life.

﴿On couches﴾: That is, beds with canopies (ḥijlah).

﴿And theirs is whatever they call for﴾: That is, whatever they wish for and ask.

﴿Peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾: That is, peace spoken by a Lord Most Merciful, meaning their Lord, glorified and exalted, greets them with peace.

Meaning of the verses:

When they are brought before Allah, glorified and exalted, for reckoning and recompense, He announces the following: The people of Paradise today are in a busy occupation, joyful. That is, they are occupied with something other than what the people of the Fire are in. They are occupied with lasting bliss, joyful, that is, enjoying themselves in delight with various kinds of food, drink, and the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn). They and their spouses are in the shade of Paradise, reclining on couches, that is, beds with canopies. For them therein, in the Abode of Peace, is fruit of every kind, variety and sort, and for them is whatever they call for, that is, whatever they wish for and ask. And greater than that is the greeting of the Lord, exalted, upon them: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾, that is, peace from Allah by speech, not by anything else, of all kinds of safety and peace.

Al-Baghawi narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While the people of Paradise are in their bliss, a light shines upon them, so they raise their heads, and behold, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has looked down upon them from above, saying: Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise. That is His saying, ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾. Then He looks at them and they look at Him, and they do not turn to anything of the bliss as long as they are looking at Him, until He veils Himself from them, and His light and His blessing remain upon them in their abodes."

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1. Affirmation of the Return (ma'ād).
2. Explanation of the bliss of Paradise.
3. Allah's peace upon the people of Paradise and their looking upon His noble Face.

*Al-yawma nakhtimu ala afwahihim* (Today We seal their mouths): i.e., when they say: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 36, verses 69–76:

Explanation of the words:

"And We did not teach him poetry": That is, We did not teach Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) poetry, so he is not a poet.

"Nor is it befitting for him": That is, it is not suitable for him, nor is it proper for him to have it.

"It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an": That is, it is not as the polytheists say, that the Qur'an is poetry. It is not — the Qur'an that Muhammad (ﷺ) recites — except a reminder, meaning an admonition, and a clear Qur'an, such that no one who hears it doubts that it is not poetry, because of the scientific truths that become apparent in it.

"That it may warn whoever is living": That is, whoever understands what he is addressed with, and they are the believers.

"And the word may be justified against the disbelievers": That is, the word of punishment is justified against the disbelievers, because they are dead and do not accept warning.

"Cattle, of which they are the owners": Al-an'am are camels, cattle and sheep.

"And We have made them subservient to them": That is, We made them subject to them and gave them mastery over them, so that they may dispose of them.

"And of them they have their mounts, and of them they eat": That is, from some of them they ride, namely camels, and from them they eat; that is, from all of them they eat.

"And for them in them are benefits and drinks": The benefits are such as wool, fleece and hair, and the drinks are milk.

"Will they not then be grateful?": That is, He rebukes them for not being grateful to Allah, the Exalted, for these blessings, by faith and obedience.

"And they have taken gods besides Allah": That is, idols which they worship, supposing that they will help them by interceding for them with Allah.

"They are not able to help them": That is, those idols cannot help them by averting punishment from them.

"And they are for them a host brought forth": That is, they cannot help them, while the polytheists themselves are a host brought forth for those gods: they defend them, protect them from anyone who would harm them. Instead of those gods helping them, they help the gods, as an army mobilized for their support.

"So let not their word grieve you": That is, you are not a messenger, and you are a poet, a soothsayer and an inventor of lies.

"Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare": That is, they only say that because of envy, while they know that you are the Messenger of Allah and that what you have brought is the truth. We will recompense them for their denial of you, their disbelief in Us, in the meeting with Us and in Our true religion.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, "And We did not teach him poetry," are a refutation of the polytheists who said the Qur'an is poetry and the Messenger is a poet. So He said, "And We did not teach him" — that is, Our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) — "poetry, nor is it befitting for him": that is, it is not proper for him nor suitable for him. "It is only a reminder": that is, what he recites is nothing but a reminder by which Allah is remembered and an admonition by which the believers are admonished, "and a clear Qur'an": clear as to the truth, manifesting the landmarks of guidance, which We sent down upon Our servant and Messenger, "that it may warn whoever is living": that is, whose heart and conscience are alive by his faith and his piety toward Allah. "And the word may be justified": that is, the word, which is punishment, "against the disbelievers", because they do not take guidance from it, so they live in misguidance and die upon it, and therefore punishment becomes due to them in the Hereafter.

His words, "Do they not see," that is, are those polytheists blind, that they have not seen the manifestations of Our power and Our favour, which necessitate worshipping Us? They are: "that We have created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, of which they are the owners," disposing of them as an owner disposes of his property. By "cattle" is meant livestock: camels, cattle and sheep. His words, "And We have made them subservient to them," that is, We subjected them to them, so that they ride them, milk them, carry loads on them, slaughter them, and eat them. Had it not been for this subjection, they would never have been able to do so.

His words, "And for them in them are benefits and drinks": the benefits are such as wool, fleece and hair; "drinks" is the plural of "mashrab," and these are the milks in their udders, which they milk and drink. His words, "Will they not then be grateful?": He rebukes them for consuming the blessings and not being grateful for them, and being grateful to Allah for them is faith in Him and the affirmation of His oneness in worship. His words, "And they have taken gods besides Allah": that is, those polytheists took gods, which are their idols that they worship, "perhaps they will be helped," that is, hoping for their help, and that by their intercession for them with Allah, the Exalted, as they claim. The Exalted said, refuting this hope and cutting it off from them: "They are not able to help them," because they are idols that neither hear, nor see, nor benefit, nor harm. His words, "And they are for them a host brought forth": that is, while the polytheists are themselves a host of those idols, brought forth, and they defend them, protect them and become angry for their sake. So how could one who is in need of your help help you?

His words, the Exalted: "So let not their word grieve you": that is, do not grieve over what your people say, that you are not a messenger, that you are a poet, a sorcerer, a soothsayer, and other such falsehoods. "Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare": We will recompense them for their false speech and seize them for their lying and fabrication against you, just as We know that they said what they said only out of envy of you. Otherwise, they know that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that you are neither a sorcerer, nor a poet, nor a madman; but envy, enmity and arrogance have driven them to what they say.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood, and that the Qur'an is a reminder and not poetry, as the falsifiers claim.

2. The wisdom behind the revelation of the Qur'an is that the Messenger warn with it those among the living who have faith.

3. Clarification of the error of those who recite the Qur'an over the dead while leaving the living without reciting it to them as admonition, guidance, teaching and reminder.

4. The obligation to mention blessings and to be grateful for them by acknowledging them, spending them in pleasing their Giver, and praising Him for them.

5. Clarification of the folly of the polytheists in worshipping idols, hoping for their help, while they are a mobilized host defending them lest anyone harm them.

*Man yuhyi al-'izama wa hiya rameem* (﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾): meaning when they have crumbled and rotted away.

*Min al-shajar al-akhdar naran* (﴿from the green tree, fire﴾): meaning from the trees al-Mirkh and al-'Affar, one of which is rubbed against the other until fire ignites.

*Bi-qadirin 'ala an yakhluqa mithlahum* (﴿is He not able to create the likes of them?﴾): meaning the likes of human beings.

*Bala* (﴿Yes indeed﴾): meaning He is able to do that, since the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind.

*Idha arada shay'an* (﴿When He intends a thing﴾): meaning when He brings a thing into existence and creates it.

*Biyadihi malakutu* (﴿in whose hand is the dominion﴾): meaning the sovereignty of everything. The letter *ta'* was added to intensify the greatness and vastness of the dominion.

*Wa ilayhi turja'un* (﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾): meaning you will be brought back after death, and that is in the Hereafter.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to establish the belief in the Resurrection and recompense, a belief on which the guidance and reform of a person largely depend. Allah, exalted is He, said in response to al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, when he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) holding a bone, crushed it and scattered it, and said, "Do you claim, O Muhammad, that Allah will resurrect this?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Yes. He will cause you to die, then bring you back to life, then gather you to Hell." These verses were revealed: ﴿Did not man see that We created him from a sperm-drop, and behold, he is an open adversary?﴾ That is, does he who knows that We created him from a despised water and shaped him into a man deny the Resurrection? ﴿Behold, he is an open adversary﴾ means he is one who disputes with Us, opposes Us, associates others with Us, and denies that We will bring the dead to life and resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection. How can he be so blind and show such ugly ignorance? For the One who is able to originate creation is rationally able to restore it, and restoration is easier for Him.

His saying, ﴿And he presents Us with an example﴾, means this denier of the Resurrection set up an example for Us, which is his denial that We are able to resurrect. He made Our restoring of creation a strange and wondrous matter when he said, ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾, that is, when they have crumbled and rotted away. ﴿And forgets his own creation﴾ from a worthless water, and how Allah made him a complete human who argues and disputes. If he had remembered the origin of his existence, he would have been ashamed to deny the revival of bones that are decayed and crumbled. Why then does he say, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say: He will give them life who brought them into being the first time﴾, is the clear and evident rational analogy (*qiyas*), for it is self-evident that whoever brought something into existence from nothing is able to bring the like of it into existence again. His saying, ﴿and He is Knower of every creation﴾, means that knowledge and power, when combined, make it easy to bring back what has been annihilated after it once existed. This is especially so because the One who originated existence from non-existence is the One who informs us of the restoration and of His power over it.

This is a decisive proof (*burhan*), and the second proof is in His saying: ﴿He who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it.﴾ That is, fire, which you ignite. The basis of the argument is that if the Resurrection were rationally impossible, and it is not impossible but is necessarily going to occur, then it would not be impossible for Allah, because Allah has brought into being something that seems impossible, namely fire from water, since the green tree is water flowing through its branches, and yet fire is produced from it. This is a rational proof which reasonable people accept and never dispute.

The third proof is in His saying: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ The basis of this proof is that we look at the seven heavens and the wondrous creation within them, and at the earth and what is in it, and then we look at the human being and find him to be nothing when compared with the heavens and the earth. So we judge that the One who created the heavens and the earth in their greatness is able, by a stronger argument, to create man again after his death, decay and annihilation. For this reason Allah answered the question Himself, saying: ﴿Yes indeed, and He is the Creator, the Knower﴾, that is, the Creator of everything He wills to create, the Knower of all His creatures, nothing of them hidden from Him.

The fourth proof is in His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ The basis of this proof is that whoever's way of bringing into being whatever He wills is to say to it "Be," and it is, there is no rational reason to deny that He can bring the dead to life by the word "Be, alive," and they will be as He commands.

Finally, this convincing refutation is concluded by declaring Allah free of incapacity. He said: ﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾, that is, the sovereignty of everything, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, whether you like it or not, O human beings, whether you were deniers of the Resurrection or affirmers of it and believers in it.

**Lessons of the verses:**

1. Establishing the belief in the Resurrection and recompense through four decisive proofs.
2. The legitimacy of using rational arguments in proof and debate.
3. Declaring Allah free of incapacity, deficiency, partners, offspring, and all other imperfections.
4. Affirming that Allah, exalted is He, holds all the dominion in His hand, under His control and subjection. Therefore it is not proper to ask anything of other than Him, for He is the true Owner, and others possess no dominion.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 36, verses 77–83**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Awa lam yara al-insan* (﴿Did not man see?﴾): meaning the one who denies the Resurrection, such as al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

*Inna khalaqnahu min nutfah* (﴿that We created him from a sperm-drop﴾): meaning from semen, until We made him a strong man.

*Fa-idha huwa khasim mubin* (﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾): meaning he is intensely contentious and clear in his denial of the Resurrection.

*Wa daraba lana mathalan* (﴿And he presents Us with an example﴾): meaning concerning this. He took a bone and crumbled it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying, "Will your Lord bring this back to life?"

*Wa nasiya khalqahu* (﴿and forgets his own creation﴾): meaning that he was created from a despised water, and then became a man who argues. Whoever is able to create the first time is able to create again.

*Man yuhyi al-'izama wa hiya rameem* (﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾): meaning when they have crumbled and rotted away.

*Min al-shajar al-akhdar naran* (﴿from the green tree, fire﴾): meaning from the trees al-Mirkh and al-'Affar, one of which is rubbed against the other until fire ignites.

*Bi-qadirin 'ala an yakhluqa mithlahum* (﴿is He not able to create the likes of them?﴾): meaning the likes of human beings.

*Bala* (﴿Yes indeed﴾): meaning He is able to do that, since the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind.

*Idha arada shay'an* (﴿When He intends a thing﴾): meaning when He brings a thing into existence and creates it.

*Biyadihi malakutu* (﴿in whose hand is the dominion﴾): meaning the sovereignty of everything. The letter *ta'* was added to intensify the greatness and vastness of the dominion.

*Wa ilayhi turja'un* (﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾): meaning you will be brought back after death, and that is in the Hereafter.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to establish the belief in the Resurrection and recompense, a belief on which the guidance and reform of a person largely depend. These verses were revealed: ﴿Did not man see that We created him from a sperm-drop, and behold, he is an open adversary?﴾ That is, does he who knows that We created him from a despised water and shaped him into a man deny the Resurrection? ﴿Behold, he is an open adversary﴾ means he is one who disputes with Us, opposes Us, associates others with Us, and denies that We will bring the dead to life and resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection. How can he be so blind and show such ugly ignorance? For the One who is able to originate creation is rationally able to restore it, and restoration is easier for Him.

His saying, ﴿And he presents Us with an example﴾, means this denier of the Resurrection set up an example for Us, which is his denial that We are able to resurrect. He made Our restoring of creation a strange and wondrous matter when he said, ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾, that is, when they have crumbled and rotted away. ﴿And forgets his own creation﴾ from a worthless water, and how Allah made him a complete human who argues and disputes. If he had remembered the origin of his existence, he would have been ashamed to deny the revival of bones that are decayed and crumbled. Why then does he say, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say: He will give them life who brought them into being the first time﴾, is the clear and evident rational analogy (*qiyas*), for it is self-evident that whoever brought something into existence from nothing is able to bring the like of it into existence again. His saying, ﴿and He is Knower of every creation﴾, means that knowledge and power, when combined, make it easy to bring back what has been annihilated after it once existed. This is especially so because the One who originated existence from non-existence is the One who informs us of the restoration and of His power over it.

This is a decisive proof (*burhan*), and the second proof is in His saying: ﴿He who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it.﴾ That is, fire, which you ignite. The basis of the argument is that if the Resurrection were rationally impossible, and it is not impossible but is necessarily going to occur, then it would not be impossible for Allah, because Allah has brought into being something that seems impossible, namely fire from water, since the green tree is water flowing through its branches, and yet fire is produced from it. This is a rational proof which reasonable people accept and never dispute.

The third proof is in His saying: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ The basis of this proof is that we look at the seven heavens and the wondrous creation within them, and at the earth and what is in it, and then we look at the human being and find him to be nothing when compared with the heavens and the earth. So we judge that the One who created the heavens and the earth in their greatness is able, by a stronger argument, to create man again after his death, decay and annihilation. For this reason Allah answered the question Himself, saying: ﴿Yes indeed, and He is the Creator, the Knower﴾, that is, the Creator of everything He wills to create, the Knower of all His creatures, nothing of them hidden from Him.

The fourth proof is in His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ The basis of this proof is that whoever's way of bringing into being whatever He wills is to say to it "Be," and it is, there is no rational reason to deny that He can bring the dead to life by the word "Be, alive," and they will be as He commands.

Finally, this convincing refutation is concluded by declaring Allah free of incapacity. He said: ﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾, that is, the sovereignty of everything, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, whether you like it or not, O human beings, whether you were deniers of the Resurrection or affirmers of it and believers in it.
